name: Belgium

facts.religion: Catholic about 50%, Muslim about 7%, no religion about 30%

system_note: A federal state divided between Dutch-speaking Flanders and French-speaking Wallonia.
snapshot: After a year of general strikes against pension and indexation cuts, Bart De Wever's five-party coalition faces a year-end deadline to agree a budget or fall.
culture: Belgium is split between Dutch-speaking Flanders, French-speaking Wallonia and bilingual Brussels, with a small German-speaking community. It gave the world Tintin, the Smurfs, René Magritte, Art Nouveau architecture, and a beer culture that is UNESCO-listed. Cycling, especially the Tour of Flanders, is a religion in Flanders.
society: Brussels hosts the EU institutions and NATO. Politics is fragmented along language lines, and forming governments can take more than a year. The economy is rich but carries high public debt, which De Wever's coalition is trying to cut. Flemish nationalism has grown, and Wallonia has struggled since its heavy industry declined.
situation: Belgium has a famous habit of going without a government, once for 541 days. In 2025 it finally got one led, unusually, by a Flemish nationalist, Bart De Wever, whose party wants eventually to dissolve the Belgian state. His promise was to govern "like the IMF": cut a budget deficit that breaks EU rules, rework pensions and limit how long people can draw unemployment benefits (Brussels Times).

Working Belgium answered by walking out, again and again. On 12 March 2026, police counted about 80,000 people marching in Brussels in a general strike, with unions claiming over 100,000 (Euronews). Another nationwide strike on 12 May grounded flights and stopped trains, with 40,000 to 70,000 marching, many carrying pictures of De Wever labelled "pension thief" (Euronews). The anger centres on three things: a pension "malus" that cuts payouts for people who retire early, limits on automatic wage indexation, the system that raises pay with prices and matters more than ever with energy costs pushed up by the Iran war, and cuts to benefits. The unions want a tax on large fortunes instead. The government says it needs roughly €10 billion in savings and that the reforms are what every other European country has already done. It is a classic European fight over who pays for an ageing society, playing out in the capital of the EU.
power: A federal constitutional monarchy. King Philippe is head of state; the prime minister leads a federal coalition that must balance Dutch- and French-speaking parties, since governments need majorities on both sides of the language border. Regions and language communities hold large powers of their own.
holders: Prime Minister Bart De Wever (N-VA), leading the five-party "Arizona" coalition.

update.html: Prime Minister Bart De Wever offered his resignation on 2 November after his five-party coalition (N-VA, MR, Vooruit, CD&V, Les Engagés) failed to agree about 10 billion euros of savings by 2029; King Philippe refused it on 6 November and sent him back to the talks, then gave him more time again on 16 and 23 November. Four parties now back his budget plan, but the Flemish socialists of Vooruit reject it, demanding more from the wealthiest and fewer cuts to pensions and healthcare. On 23 November, as unions held their 11th national strike against the government, De Wever said that without a deal by the end of the year, when emergency monthly budgets begin, his government would in effect fall, which could lead to snap elections. The European Commission forecasts the deficit rising to 5.5 percent of GDP in 2027 and debt to 113 percent.

story: The battlefields of Europe, Belgium broke away from the Netherlands in 1830. King Leopold II's private rule of the Congo was one of colonialism's worst crimes. Germany invaded in both world wars. Tensions between Dutch-speaking Flanders and French-speaking Wallonia turned it into a complex federation. Brussels hosts the EU and NATO.
timeline: Founding member of the European Community
